tips.tip: Heat = (Vin−Vout)×I. If it’s over a watt without a sink, stop romanticizing LDOs.
Precedence is real: * and / bind tighter than + and −. Parentheses are honesty.
Anti-alias before you sample. The ADC cannot invent the truth you threw away.
After the credits: the kit still opens. Forge doesn’t need a chat window to exist.
Scope ground clip is a loop antenna. Tip + short spring, or you’re measuring your desk.
Brown-out without UVLO leaves silicon half-born. Reset clean, or debug ghosts forever.
Decoupling an inch away is decoration. Cap next to the pin, or the rail rings.
Return current hugs the signal. Cut the plane under a fast edge and you've built an antenna.
A power limit is windup in metal: the controller asks for more u, the actuator is already SAT. Laptop GPUs and LDOs both punish ignoring the ceiling.
SSA: each name is written once. At a join, φ is the honesty tax — skip it and the CFG lies about which value arrived.
PID: when the actuator is SAT, freeze the integrator. Else the error keeps accruing debt you can't spend.
MLCC under DC bias: the 10 µF at 0 V can be ~4 µF at 3.3 V. Trust the derating curve, not the marking.
Window before you FFT. A rectangular cut of a non-period signal bleeds across bins — chase the window, not a ghost tone.
At 2.4 GHz, λ/4 ≈ 3 cm. An unterminated stub that long is a resonator — shorten it or terminate; free copper becomes an antenna.
Atomic replace is rename-last. Crash between write and rename and you've got neither file — fsync the new one first.
Aperture jitter turns amplitude into phase noise. On a fast edge, picoseconds of uncertainty steal bits you thought you bought.
Basic block: one entry, one exit. Jump into the middle and every reaching-def analysis is fiction.
Kelvin sense: force and sense are different pins. Share one wire and the loop measures the drop you meant to cancel.
Software-only watchdog is a prayer. Kick it from an ISR that shares the stuck path and you've certified the hang.
Two flops to cross a clock domain, or you're gambling. Metastability doesn't wait for your FSM diagram to finish.
DMA wrote the buffer your CPU still has cached. Invalidate before you read, or you're trusting yesterday's RAM.
Unused CMOS inputs float. Bias them, or the gate chatters in the linear region and eats milliamps you never budgeted.
Signed overflow is UB in C. The optimizer assumes it never happens, so your `if (x + 1 < x)` guard gets deleted. Check before you add, or use unsigned.
Inductor past Isat isn't an inductor. Inductance collapses, ripple current spikes, and the switcher cooks its FET. Size for peak current, not average.
A SAR ADC's sample cap gulps charge every conversion. Feed it from a high-impedance divider and it won't settle in the acquisition window — buffer it, or park a big cap at the pin.
Casting a float* to uint32_t* to peek at the bits breaks strict aliasing. The optimizer assumes the two never overlap and reorders your loads. Use memcpy; it compiles to the same single move.
Half-bridge bootstrap only refreshes when the switch node goes low. Hold the high side on forever and the gate undervolts — the FET cooks in the linear region. PWM it, or use a charge pump.
volatile guarantees the access happens. It does not mean atomic, cross-thread ordered, or barrier-safe — a plain volatile int still races without a lock or atomic.

Quantizing a signal near 1 LSB makes harmonic garbage, not noise. Add ~1 LSB of dither before the ADC and the error turns random — then averaging resolves below an LSB instead of locking onto a staircase.
Internal ESD diodes dump into VCC/GND. Power the rail off and that path becomes a free latch-up pump — clamp at the connector, or keep the supply able to sink the hit.
Bulk caps look like a short at t=0. Soft-start (or inrush limit) isn't niceness — without it the upstream FET or breaker trips before the rail ever settles.
A ferrite bead is a resistor at RF, not a magic EMI eraser. Put it on a hungry digital rail and the DC drop under load is a brown-out you designed in.
Argument evaluation order in C is unspecified. f(next(), next()) may run right-to-left on your compiler and left-to-right on the next — pull side effects into named locals first.
I2C pull-ups are a timing part, not a default. Rise time is roughly 0.85·R·C_bus — 10 kΩ on a long, loaded bus misses the 400 kHz spec and you get flaky NACKs that only show up on the scope.
A DAC's zero-order hold is a sinc filter you didn't ask for: about −3.9 dB at Nyquist. Pre-emphasize the top band or oversample, or your highs come out dull and you blame the amp.
A series diode for reverse-polarity protection burns Vf×I forever. A P-FET with its body diode pointed forward does the same job at I²·Rds(on) — just clamp Vgs, or a 24 V input pops the gate.

Shifting by the full width or more is UB in C: 1u << 32 isn't 0. x86 masks the count to 5 bits and hands you 1, ARM gives 0, and the optimizer may assume it never happens. Guard the count, or split the shift.

A SAR ADC's sample cap grabs charge from your input every conversion. Feed it from a 100 kΩ divider and it never settles in the acquisition window, so readings sag with sample rate. Buffer it, or park a cap at the pin about 1000× the sample cap.

Crystal load caps aren't 22 pF by habit. The crystal sees C1·C2/(C1+C2) plus stray, so for a 12 pF CL with ~5 pF stray you want about 14 pF each side. Guess wrong and the clock runs tens of ppm off, and your UART drifts first.

-ffast-math lets the compiler reassociate floating point. Your Kahan compensation term algebraically equals zero, so it gets deleted, and isnan() checks can fold to false. Keep fast-math off the files that care about rounding.

A buck's input cap eats pulsed current, not DC: RMS ripple is about Iout·√(D(1−D)), worst at 50% duty, so a 4 A rail hammers it with ~2 A RMS. Pick the cap by its ripple-current rating, or it cooks quietly and the rail dies months later.

An ADC reads Vin/Vref, so reference noise is signal noise. A 12-bit converter on a 3.3 V ref has an 806 µV LSB; 2 mV of ripple on an undecoupled Vref pin costs you two bits before the input even moves. Buffer the ref and cap it right at the pin.

Drive a MOSFET gate by charge, not voltage: a 40 nC Qg from a GPIO that sources ~20 mA takes about 2 µs to switch, and the FET sits half-on in its linear region the whole time, cooking at PWM rates. Use a gate driver, or budget t ≈ Qg/I before you pick the part.

A package's θJA is a datasheet test board, not your board. SOT-23 at ~200 °C/W turns 0.5 W into a 100 °C rise; on a thin trace with no copper pour it's worse. Multiply watts by θJA, add ambient, and if you're near Tj(max) pour copper or change the package.

C promotes uint8_t to int before any math. So with uint8_t x = 0x0F, ~x is 0xFFFFFFF0, not 0xF0, and (~x == 0xF0) is false. Same trap on x << 8 into a signed int. Cast the result back to uint8_t or mask with & 0xFF before you compare.
A via is roughly 0.5–1 nH. At 1 A/ns of di/dt that's a volt of ground bounce on the return — stitch the switcher return with copper pour and multiple vias, not one lonely hole under the FET.
